blocks.c: "The Record," said the clerk, "is the volume in use at the material time."

"Both are in use. Here's this morning's entry in the black one, timed 03:14, my hand. Here's this morning's entry in the blue one, timed 03:20, her hand. Both dated today. Both maintained. Both on the premises."
"The blue volume is a superseded volume."

"Show me where the lease says superseded volumes stop being current." I put my finger on page ten. "It says the volume in use. It doesn't say the volume issued. You wrote this in 1874 and there was one book and it never occurred to you that there could be two, because it has never once occurred to you that there could be two of anything, which is why you have spent a hundred and fifty-one years with one caretaker and one clerk and one book, alone, in a basement, doing paperwork."

"The Record," said the clerk, and something in its voice cracked like a photocopier taking a staple, "is the volume in use at the material time, and if two volumes are in use at the material time then both are the Record, and a Caretaker who maintains the Record is a Caretaker in occupation, and—"
The window blind rattled, once, in no wind.
Wen put her hand flat on the counter next to mine. Her palm was wet. I looked at her and she was grinning like a lunatic.
"Say it," she said. "Say the whole sentence. You know how this works. It has to be said out loud in front of the landlord and it has to be true."
